reasoning_traces.think:
The rate-limit coverage problem is modeled as a binary classification task over API routes. With 71 protected routes out of 176 total, the coverage ratio R = 71/176 ≈ 0.403. This implies 40.3% of routes are rate-limited, while 59.7% are not. The protection mechanism is per-route, using three distinct limiter functions: consumeRateLimit (IP/user-keyed), consumePublicFormRateLimit (public form), and requirePremiumApiRateLimited (auth-gated). These functions define a layered access control system. The absence of middleware-level rate limiting indicates a distributed enforcement strategy. Cron routes (24 files) are excluded from rate limiting due to bearer token auth, and admin routes (9 files) lack rate limits despite requiring auth. The failure mode occurs when unprotected routes are subject to abuse or DoS attacks. The mathematical structure supports a probabilistic model in GSI and a state-transition kernel in GSE.
